title: Lights of the High Pass
summary: Guide trekkers through a blizzard by setting a lodge turbine’s frequency so a choke and a capacitor give its lamps the right current.
subject: physics
ncertRef: Section 7.4, AC voltage applied to an inductor
concepts: Current lags in L and leads in C by 90°
No average power in a pure L or C
learningOutcome: The student can find the frequency at which a choke or a capacitor passes a set current, predict what a change of frequency does to each, and use their quarter-cycle phase and zero average power.

levels.title: The trail choke
levels.adds: Baseline: a choke’s reactance X_L = 2πfL sets the lamps’ current, I = V/X_L, and grows with frequency (Ex 7.3, Example 7.2).
hints: X_L = V/I: first find the reactance the lamps need.
Then f = X_L/(2πL), with L in henry (mH × 10⁻³).
A faster turbine means a bigger X_L and less current.

levels.title: The porch capacitor
levels.adds: New idea: a capacitor’s reactance X_C = 1/(2πfC) falls as the frequency rises, so a faster turbine passes more current (Ex 7.4, Example 7.4).
hints: X_C = V/I for the current the beacon needs.
Then f = 1/(2πC X_C), with C in farad (µF × 10⁻⁶).
A faster turbine means a smaller X_C and more current: the opposite of a choke.

levels.title: Both lamps
levels.adds: Apply it: a choke and a capacitor on one supply react oppositely to frequency, so only one frequency suits both lamps (Examples 7.3, 7.5).
hints: The trail lamps set a highest frequency: f ≤ V/(2πL I_trail).
The beacon sets a lowest frequency: f ≥ I_beacon/(2πCV).
Pick the whole number between the two.

levels.title: Steady light
levels.adds: New idea: L and C pass current a quarter cycle out of step with the voltage and take no average power; X = R makes the currents equal (Ex 7.5).
hints: Equal currents need the reactance to equal the dropper’s resistance.
For a choke f = R/(2πL); for a capacitor f = 1/(2πRC).
A quarter cycle apart, one lamp peaks just as the other goes dark.

misconceptions: A capacitor blocks the current more at high frequency
An inductor absorbs power from an AC source
The current in an inductor leads the voltage
Reactance does not depend on the frequency
